title: Claude in biology labs: Biomni, MozzareLLM, and others
summary: Anthropic describes three cases: Biomni (Stanford) completed a GWAS analysis in 20 minutes in an initial trial and suggested new transcription factors in embryonic development; MozzareLLM (MIT and Whitehead) interprets gene clusters from CRISPR screens; a third lab is still testing. This is an Anthropic account without independent evaluation; some figures are estimates.

evidence.tested: Biomni's case studies (GWAS analysis, cloning design blind-evaluated against a postdoc, embryonic-tissue cell analysis) were checked by the Biomni team, citing a bioRxiv preprint; MozzareLLM was assessed qualitatively by its lab, with no quantitative benchmark.
evidence.unknown: The article says the validation is not independent, some figures are estimates (such as the three-week human comparison), and Biomni cannot yet do everything out of the box.
evidence.ai_role: A Claude-powered agent (Biomni) analysed GWAS and embryonic cell data and suggested transcription factors; a Claude-powered system (MozzareLLM) interprets gene clusters from CRISPR screens.
